title: CardCorpus static API manifest
description: Where everything is: the files, how a pointer finds what it names, how a picture id becomes a url, and how many of each thing there are.

description.description: What the dataset is, in a sentence.

version.description: The version of the shape these files follow (semver).

pictures.description: How a picture id becomes a url: fill `{id}` and `{width}`, one of `widths`, into `sized` (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pictures).

sized.description: The url of a copy at one of `widths`, with `{id}` and `{width}`.

widths.description: The widths a sized copy comes in, in pixels.

latest.description: A set's latest daily prices, with `{set}`.

sets.description: Up to 64 sets' latest prices at once, with `{sets}`: their ids joined by commas.

history.description: A card's price history, with `{set}` and `{card}`.

rates.description: The day's exchange rates, to show prices in another currency.

schemas.description: The JSON Schema of what each url above answers, by its key here: a file in this tree.

latest.description: The schema of a set's prices.

sets.description: The schema of many sets' prices.

history.description: The schema of a card's price history.

rates.description: The schema of the exchange rates.

docs.description: Where the documentation is, as Markdown: each a path in this tree, beside index.json.

guide.description: The guide: the ideas the files share (pointers, copies, links, pictures, prices), which the schemas' descriptions cite by section.

reference.description: The field reference: every field of every file, generated from the schemas.

marketplaces.description: Where a card opens in a marketplace: fill a product id from marketplaces/ into `tcgplayer` or `cardmarket` (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#marketplace-ids).

catalogs.description: The catalogs, in the order lists use. A catalog is one language's product line, with its own sets and numbering: `english`, `japanese`, `zh-hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-hant` (Traditional Chinese), `thai`, `indonesian`, `korean`, `french`, `german`, `italian`, `spanish`, `portuguese`, `latin-american-spanish` (Latin American Spanish), `dutch`, `russian` and `polish`. Its `language` is that language; a box such as the Pikachu World Collection holds cards in others, each with its own `language`. Each has its list of sets (sets/{catalog}.json) and of cards (cards/{catalog}.json).

id.description: The catalog's id, the first part of its sets' ids: `english`.

language.description: The language most of its cards are printed in: `en`.

languages.description: Every language a card of it is printed in, the one with the most cards first: `en` and then the Pikachu World Collection's other languages for the english catalog.

setCount.description: How many sets; always present, 0 included.

cardCount.description: How many cards; always present, 0 included.

variantCount.description: How many variants; always present, 0 included.

counts.description: How many of each thing the files hold, each named for its unit.

additionalProperties.description: How many there are of the thing the key names; always present, 0 included.

files.description: Every file, as a pattern whose `{…}` a pointer's ids fill, with its JSON Schema.

file.description: The file's path under /v1, with `{…}` for the ids that pick one.

pointers.description: How to find what a pointer points at, by its `$kind` (https://pokemon.cardcorpus.com/v1/docs/guide.md#pointers): fill `file` from the pointer's ids and open it, then walk `path` in order, at each step picking from `list` the item whose `match` field equals the pointer's `by` field.

file.description: The file to open, with `{…}` filled from the pointer's ids.

path.description: The steps to walk, in order.

match.description: The field of each item to compare.

by.description: The pointer's field to compare it with.
